sn12.31:3.1: The Buddha has already given a brief answer to the question. Here he asks for a detailed response, presumably as a teaching method: the dialogue was probably in front of an assembly.
sn12.31:3.2: Sāriputta hesitates, according to the commentary, because he is unsure of the mode of analysis that the Buddha wants him to pursue.
sn12.31:7.1: See [mn38:9.1](), where “this has come to be” refers to dependently originated consciousness. This draws on the original context of the question, which was asked by a contemplative brahmin from a school that identified the cosmic divinity with the state of purified formless consciousness experienced in deep meditation.
sn12.31:7.4: “Originated with that as fuel” is at [mn38:9.3](), cementing the connection between these two texts.
